pull_request.title: feat: add RISC-V architecture support
pull_request.body:
Mount the RISC-V architecture in the verification build alongside x86 and add the specification instance that the shared address-space model needs.

- Mount `irq`, `mm`, and `timer` for `riscv64` and select the `RiscvArch` specification instance through `CurrentArch`.
- Export the Sv48 paging constants and implement `PagingConstsTrait` with the same spec and exec layout as x86.
- Add verified `PageTableEntry` operations and the `PageTableEntryTrait` implementation, including flag parsing and the `is_last` mask rewrite avoids Verus's BitOr specification dependency-order issue.
- Add `ostd/specs/arch/riscv` with the address-space model and the transitional `lemma_arch_specific_consts_properties`, which still depends on the shared `axiom_current_paging_consts_hardcoded`.
- Add `riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf` and `loongarch64-unknown-none-softfloat` to `rust-toolchain.toml`, and update the RISC-V `timer` and `task` items shared with `cpu` and `kvirt_area` to build on that target.
pull_request.bodyHTML:
Mount the RISC-V architecture in the verification build alongside x86 and add the specification instance that the shared address-space model needs.

  • Mount irq, mm, and timer for riscv64 and select the RiscvArch specification instance through CurrentArch.
  • Export the Sv48 paging constants and implement PagingConstsTrait with the same spec and exec layout as x86.
  • Add verified PageTableEntry operations and the PageTableEntryTrait implementation, including flag parsing and the is_last mask rewrite avoids Verus's BitOr specification dependency-order issue.
  • Add ostd/specs/arch/riscv with the address-space model and the transitional lemma_arch_specific_consts_properties, which still depends on the shared axiom_current_paging_consts_hardcoded.
  • Add riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf and loongarch64-unknown-none-softfloat to rust-toolchain.toml, and update the RISC-V timer and task items shared with cpu and kvirt_area to build on that target.

review_comments.body:
I checked the latest Asterinas. `set_prop()` was removed in [this refactoring](https://github.com/asterinas/asterinas/commit/c77c2686d85a1952683db21d7bd7e287f4e8b883), and the current `protect()` only updates mapped entries.

The old RISC-V implementation did violate the trait's documented no-op behavior for absent entries. However, `protect()` already guarded against absent entries, while `new_page()` relied on `set_prop()` to initialize VALID. So this was a contract inconsistency, but I have not identified a runtime failure caused by it.

review_comments.body:
I tested this. Replacing the shifts with `paddr >> 2` in the two spec functions fails verification.

The expressions are equivalent for 4 KiB-aligned addresses, but the current contracts also allow unaligned addresses. For example, with `paddr = 8`, `(paddr >> 12) << 10` gives `0`, whereas `paddr >> 2` gives `2`, setting the PTE's Readable bit.

So we cannot directly use `>> 2` under the current contracts.
